title: Hamzanama (Book of Hamza), Akbar's illustrated manuscript
summary: The Hamzanama was an illustrated manuscript of the adventures of Hamza commissioned by the Mughal emperor Akbar and painted in the court's new painting studio, directed by two Iranian masters. Work is thought to have begun around 1562 and ran to about 1577. It originally had about 1,400 illustrations, of which fewer than 200 survive.

uncertainty.note: The V&A says work is thought to have begun in about 1562 and gives the painted span 1562-1577; most authorities agree on 'about 1562 and 1577'.

where.modern_name: Victoria and Albert Museum, London, United Kingdom (holding museum; labelled proxy pin, not the place of making)
where.historical_name: Mughal court workshop, Mughal Empire (city of making not stated in opened sources)

importance.justification: The first major project of the Mughal court's new painting studio, with about 1,400 illustrations planned (V&A).

sources.title: Wikidata item Q213322 (Victoria and Albert Museum), coordinate location (P625)

reviewer_note: Pin is the V&A as a holding museum (labelled proxy); the opened pages name no city of making. The V&A article also notes MAK Vienna holds about 60 folios. Counts differ by source: V&A says fewer than 200 survive; hamzanama.org says 14 volumes of about 100 pages. The Met pages returned 429 so were not used. Second publisher hamzanama.org is a project of a non-profit foundation, class other; the V&A supplies the institutional source.
